title: Vendor-specific adapter boundaries
description: One entry per concrete agent runtime this platform can dispatch a work unit to. `offers` is the MEASURED-TRUE set and `refuses` the MEASURED-FALSE set; a capability in NEITHER list is UNMEASURED and negotiation treats it as a refusal with reason capability-unmeasured. The three-state split is the mechanism behind the spec's 'do not pretend full interchangeability' - an adapter can only be trusted for what somebody actually measured.
how_to_extend: Add the capability id to `offers` or `refuses` together with a provenance line in CAPABILITY-REGISTRY.json or in this entry's `notes`. Never add to `offers` on the strength of a vendor's documentation alone; the estate has measured three separate cases where the documented behaviour was inert (codex --sandbox, hooks.json $schema, MCP disable-scope).

notes: sandbox.enforced REFUSED: Windows has no native OS-level process sandbox for this runtime; risky execution is routed to WSL2, the docker MCP or a remote sandbox instead. Containment is a routing decision, not a runtime guarantee.

schema.typed_output REFUSED: a subagent can be ASKED for a shape but the runtime does not constrain the emission, so the caller must validate. The AND-gate's third limb is therefore always caller-side on this adapter.
transport.detached_child OFFERED via run_in_background/longrun - permitted only with an explicit barrier (see ADAPTER-CONTRACT.md).
Every value here is LEDGER-RECORDED from the 2026-07-18 rail smoke-test (~/.claude/agents/codex.md) and was NOT re-measured by this build unit.

fs.write OFFERED only under --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox, because --sandbox workspace-write is inert on codex-cli 0.144.5 / Windows. That is why sandbox.enforced is REFUSED in the same breath: the write works, the confinement does not.

mcp.tools REFUSED by policy, not by absence: --ignore-user-config is mandatory (the active inventory blows the 32,767-char Windows arg limit and voids --output-schema per codex issue #15451). Declaring it refused is what makes the mcp.tools x schema.typed_output conflict visible to negotiation instead of silent.
interactive.owner_approval REFUSED: the invocation that works on this box bypasses approvals outright, so the runtime structurally cannot pause for the owner.
session.resume carries an inherited UNVERIFIED: its interaction with --ephemeral is untested.

Deliberately empty. This adapter is REACHABLE in principle (.metaswarm/external-tools.yaml can delegate to Gemini CLI) but no capability of it has been measured on this box by this unit or by any ledger entry it could cite.

Consequence, and the point of the entry: negotiation REFUSES every unit routed here with reason capability-unmeasured. An empty adapter that refuses loudly is correct; an empty adapter that inherits another vendor's capability list would be the exact 'pretend full interchangeability' failure the spec forbids.
The experiment that promotes any capability here: run the same probe used for codex-cli against gemini-cli and record the result in this file.

Exists so a unit with owner_approval_required=true has a legal destination. `human` resolves in VENDOR-REGISTRY.json with establishes_distinctness=true, so an owner review is a genuine cross-vendor review.
